Republic or the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quozon City http: l/w,vw. dilg.gov.ph OPINION N0- 30 OCT 2017 MR. MEDARDO TANDINGAN Barangay Pulot, Lagayan Abra Dear Mr. Tandingan: s. 2011 This has reference to your letter requesting the Department's legal opinion on whether you could continue to discharge the duties and functions of the Punong Barangay even after 12 August 2017. Per your letter, Mr. Leonard Donato, the elected Punong Barangay of Barangay Pulot in Lagayan, Abra was suspended until 12 August 2017. Furthermore, you represented that PB Donato is also in jail while the court hearings of his murder case is on-going. Hence, your request for legal opinion. We note that the suspension and incarceration of PB Donato took place during the hold over period under Republic Act No. 109231. Section 3 of the said law provides and we quote: SEC. 3. Hold Over.—Until their successors shall have been dulv elected and qualified, all incumbent barangay officials shall remain in office, unless sooner removed or suspended for cause. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 145, series of 2010, the Department opined that the holdover period does not constitute a separate term but merely a valid extension period during which an incumbent may legally perform the functions of his office pending the assumption of a successor. Jurisprudence is replete of cases clarifying that holdover does not affect an official's the term of office but rather only his tenure, thus: AN POSTPONING THE ocroBER 2016 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECI*IONS. AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACI' NO. 9164, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC Acr NO. 9340 AND REPUBLIC NO. 10656. PRESCRIBING ADDITIONAL RULES GOVERNING THE CONDUCT OF BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

The word term has acquired a definite meaning in jurisprudence. In several cases, we have defined term as the time during which the officer may claim to hold the office as of right, and fixes the interval after which the several incumbents shall succeed one another. term of office is not affected by the holdover. The term is fixed by statute and it dOß not change simply because the office may have become vacant, nor bæause the incumbent holds over in office nd the end f the term to and has failed to qualify r has not Term is distinguished from tenure in that an officer's tenure represents the term during which the incumbent actually holds office The tenure may be shorter (or, in case of holdover, longer) than the term for reasons within or beyond the power of the incumbent. Based on the above discussion, when Section 23 ofthe Corporation Code declares that the board of directors shall hold office for one (1) year until their successors are elected and qualified, we construe the provision to mean that the term of the members of the board of directors shall be only for one year; their term expires one year after election to the office. The holdover period that time from the lapse of one year from a members election to the Board and until his successors election and qualification is not part of the directors original term of office, nor is it a new term; the holdover period, however, constitutß part of his tenure. Corollary, when an incumbent member of the board of directors continue; to serve in a holdover capacity, it implies that the office has a fixed term, which has expired and the incumbent is holding the succeeding term. After the lapse of one year from his election as member of the VVCC Board in 1996, Makalintals term of office is deemed to have already expired. That he continued to serve in the VVCC Board in a holdover capacity cannot be considered as extending his term. To be precise, Makalintals term of office began in 1996 and expired in 1997, but, by virtue of the holdover doctrine in Section 23 of the Corporation Code, he continued to hold office until his resignation on November IO, 1998. Ihis holdover period, however, is not to be considered as part of his term, which, as declared, had already expired.2 (Emphasis Supplied) It cannot be gainsaid that the term of office of the elective barangay officials, like PB Donato, expired last November 2016 and that herein holdover period constitutes only part of their tenure as defined above. 2 G.R. No. 151969, Valle Verde, et al. vs. Africa, 04 September 2009.

With this premise, the logical view is that the cited provision of Section 44 and accordingly, Section 453 of the Local Government Code of 1991 should not be applied in the filling-up of vacancies during the holdover period. A more careful reading of the aforesaid Sections 44 and 45 reveal that they only contemplate vacancies occurring within the term of office of the local elective officials. When such vacancy is created after the expiration Of a term (such as during the holdover period), logically, there is no more unexpired term to speak of within which the successor to a vacant position must serve. However, well-settled is the rule in Statutory Construction that in case of doubt, the intent of the law is to promote right and justice. Fiat justicia ruat coelum. Since the Local Government Code of 1991 does not provide specific procedures in the filling-up of vacancy during the holdover period, such solution that promotes right and justice should be pursued. In this regard, it would be prudent for us to us go back to the provision of Section 3 of Republic Act No. 10923. Based on this provision of law, all incumbent barangay officials (e.g. Punong Barangay, Sangguniang Barangay Members) shall remain in their respective positions, subject to the happening of the following: (1) When their successors have already been duly elected and qualified; (2) Removed or suspended for cause prior to the election and qualification of their successors. Attention is invited to the number 2 scenario. Section 3 of RA 1()923 therefore also contemplates a situation wherein during the holdover period, an incumbent barangay official, may still be removed or suspended, the same grounds for permanent (Section 44) 3 SECTION 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian. — (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automatic succession provided above do not apply shall be filled by appointment in the following manner: (l) The President, through the Executive Secretary, in the case of the sangguniang panlalawigan and the sanwlniang panlungsod of highly urbanized cities and independent component cities; (2) The governor, in the case of the sangguniang panlungsod of component cities and the Sangguniang bayan; (3) The city or municipal mayor, in the case of *Ingguniang barangay, upon recommendation of the sangguniang barangay concerned. (b) Except for the sangguniang barangay, only the nominee of the political party under which the sanggunian member concerned had been elected and whose elevation to the pmition next higher in rank created the last vacancy in the sanggunian shall be appointed in the manner hereinabove provided. The appointee shall come from the same political party as that of the sanggunian member who caused the vacancy and shall serve the unexpired term of the vacant office. In the appointment herein mentioned, a nomination and a certificate of membership of the appointee from the highest official of thc political party concerned are conditions sine qua non, and any appointrnent without such nomination and certification shall be null and void ab initio and shall be a ground for administrative action against the official responsible th erefor. (c) In the permanent vacancy is caused by a sanggunian member who does not belong to any political party, the local chief executive shall, upon recommendation of the sanggunian concerned, appoint a qualified person to fill the vacancy. (d) In case of vacancy in the representation of the youth and the barangay in the sanggunian, said vacancy shall be filled automatically by the official next in rank of the organization concerned

and temporary vacancies (Section 464) enumerated under the Local Government Code of 1991. Thus, while as discussed above, Sections 44 and 45 of the Local Government Code of 1991 cover only vacancies occurring within the term of office of the local elective officials, it appears that the law, RA 1()923, by providing the number 2 scenario mentioned above. intended to apply the manner of filling-up vacancies provided under Sections 44 and 45 (for permanent vacancies) and 46 (temporary vacancies such as in the case at hand) of the Local Government Code of 1991 to vacancies created even during the holdover period, unless the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) thereafter shows a contrary intent. Accordingly, Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 states that when the punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from omce, the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Meantime, RA 109525 was approved but nevertheless, the same provision on holdover was provided. Now that your right to temporarily succeed to the position of Punong Barangay during the suspension of PB Donato has been established, the next issue that you posed is 4 SECT* ION Temporary Vacancy in the Office of the Local Chief Executive. — (a) When the governor, city or municipal mayor, or punong baranwy ternporarily incapacitated to perform his duties physical but not limited to, leave Of travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice-governor, city or municipai or the highest ranking barang.y member shall automatically exercise the B'Wers and the duties and functiorw of the local chief oncrrned, except the lx»wer to appoint. stspend, or ernploy•ecs which can only be if the of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) wcrking days. (b) Said temporary incapacity shall terminate upon submiwion to the appropriate of a written declaration by the local chief executive concerned that he has reported back to office. In cases where the temporary incapacity is due to legal causes, the local chief executive concerned shall also submit necessary documents showing that said legal causes no longer exisL (Emphasis Supplied) (c) When the incumbent local chief executive is traveling within the country but outside his territorial jurisdiction for a period not exceeding three (3) consecutive days, he may designate in writing the officer-in-charge of the said office. Such authorization shall specify thc powers and functions that the local official concerned shall exercise in the absence of the local chief executive except the power to appoint, suspend, or employees. (d) In the event, however, that the local chief executive concerned fails or refuses to such authorization, the vice- governor, the city or municipal vice-mayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member, as the case may be, shall have the right to as.sume the powers, duties, and functions of the said office on the fourth (4th) day of absence of the said local chief executive, subject to the limitations provided in subsection (c) hereof. (e) Except as provided above, the local Ch icf executive shall in no case authorize any local official to assume the powers, duties, and functions of the office, other than thc vice-governor, the city or municipal vicernayor, or the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member, as the case may be. s AN Acr POSTPONING THE OCI'OBER 2017 BARANGAY AND SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN ELECTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC Acr NO. 9164, AS AMENDED BY REPUBLIC ACF NO. 9340, REPUBLIC Acr NO. IOCA32, REPUBLIC Acr NO. 10656, AND REPUBLIC Acr NO. 10923, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES.

— can you still discharge the position of Punong Barangay after 12 August 2017, the last day of his suspension? In this regard, may we invite your attention to People of the Philippines vs. Maceda, et al.6, where the Supreme Court held and we quote: As a matter of law, when a person indicted for an offense is arrested, he is deemed placed under the custody of the law. He is placed in actual restraint of'libertv in jail so that he may bound to answer for the commission of the offense. He must detained in jail during the pendency of the case against him, unless he is authorized by the court to be released on bail or on revognizance. it that all in an final sentence can or ld o •ve or while in detention. This is a conayænce of arrest and detention. Consequently, all the accused in Criminal Cases Nos. 3350-3355 must ly confined in the Provincial jail of Antique. (Emphasis Supplied) The foregoing was reiterated by the Supreme Court in People of the Philippines vs. Jalosjos7, thus: No less than accused-appellant himself admits that like any other member of the House of Representatives "[h]e is provided with a congressional office situated at Room N-214, North Wing Building, House of Representatives Complex, Batasan Hills, Quezon City, manned by a full complement ofstaffpaid for by Congress Through [an] interdepartment coordination, he is also provided with an office at the Administration Building, New Bilibid Prison, Muntinlupa City, where he attends to his constituents. " Accused-appellant further admits that while under detention, he has filed several bills and resolutions. It also appears that he has been receiving his salaries and other monetary benefits. Succinctly stated, accused-appellant has Iren discharging his mandate as a memlær of the House of Representative consistent with the restraints upon one who is presently under detention. Beingadetainee accused- apN1ant should even have allowed the prison authorities at the National Pentientiary to—orm these acts. (Emphasis Supplied) Based on the foregoing, confinement in jail may be considered as a temporary incapacity which gives rise to temporary vacancy in an elective office under Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991. Let it be noted that a temporary incapacity which gives rise to temporary vacancy in an elective office under the aforesaid provision of the Local Government Code of 1991 may be due to physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office. G.R. No. 89591-96, 24 January 2000. 7 Supra.

(7 There being a temporary vacancy in the position of Punong Barangay after 12 August 2017 due to PB Donato's continued detention in jail, as discussed above, the filling- up thereof shall be in accordance with Section 46 of the Local Government Code of 1991 , even during the holdover period, unless the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) thereafter shows a contrarv intent- We hope to have guided you accordingly.
